claims.text: The as-cast eutectic AlCoCrFeNi alloy has a lamellar microstructure.
Aging at 600°C for 1 hour followed by rapid quenching will form precipitates at and near the lamellar interfaces.
The precipitates produced by the treatment will be nanoscale and coherent.
The interfacial nanoscale precipitates will impede dislocation motion.
Impeded dislocation motion will increase the alloy's strength.
The precipitate-containing lamellar microstructure will maintain or enhance its ability to accommodate plastic deformation.
Maintained or enhanced plastic-deformation accommodation will increase ductility.
The treatment will increase room-temperature yield strength by approximately 20% relative to the untreated as-cast alloy.
The treatment will increase room-temperature uniform elongation by approximately 15% relative to the untreated as-cast alloy.
Deviating from the specified temperature, aging time, or quenching rate may produce non-uniform or overaged precipitates.
Non-uniform or overaged precipitates could negate the predicted strength and ductility improvements.
The magnitude of the mechanical-property improvements depends on achieving the correct precipitate size and uniformity.
